Because the fish needs to move.
Current leading edge 47: rows 48–62 are p (flood). Fish's water: rows 37–47 are S? S@37=18. Pool: S continues down to row 47 (23 wide), row 48 is p? So the flood is eating at row 47/48. Next wave is at next LEFT/RIGHT. When the chamber's water is exhausted, the flood will reach the fish's row → game over or eject.
Hmm, wait, actually the flood's "drain" converts S→B, and the "fill" converts B→p — but which cells become p? Looking at the wave data: row 57: S 23→7 (partial drain, cols 31–53 partially? no — row 57 is B 41 + S 23: S is cols 31–53; after: S 7, B 57: S 16 cells → B). Row 58: S 23→0, B 34→64 (all B). Row 59: B 35→32, p 0→32 (B→p, 32 cells = cols 1–32?? left side + …). Row 60: B 41→10, p 0→54. So each wave: the row above the front is drained (S→B, full width of cols 1–63), the row at the front becomes partially p (32–54 cells: from the left edge up to around col 32–63? row 60 p=54: cols 10–63; row 59 p=32: cols 1–32?? asymmetric).
In the current image: the purple band is at rows ~55–62, the lower portion of the pool is p, the pool above (rows 43–54) is still S, the fish's pocket is intact. The fish is below the gap ✓ (44).
Strategy unchanged: wait for the surge. But should I also consider that the "eject" might require the fish to be exactly below the gap (44–46 ✓ done).
Now: do one LEFT (or RIGHT) swim to trigger a wave, and observe the chamber's drain + fish. The fish will move away from below the gap — that's fine, I can reposition later. Actually, which direction? The reflow pushed the fish rightward (40→46). If the eject pushes the fish up through the gap, the fish needs to be at cols 43–47 at the moment of the eject. A wave from a swim moves the fish ±8 — the fish ends up at 36 (L) or 52 (R), no longer below the gap. Hmm. But maybe the eject happens when the last wave hits, at which point the fish's position at that moment matters.
Alternative: maybe I don't need to trigger a swim at all — no-ops are free and the flood is stationary. But then nothing progresses; the eject never occurs. The eject is probably triggered when the flood fills the chamber (needs waves = needs swims).
So: I must swim, but I need to end up below the gap at the moment of the final wave. The drain consumes about 3–4 more waves. Sequence: swim, reposition, swim, reposition… each swim = 1 wave + fish move. I can interleave: e.g., RIGHT (fish→52, wave), LEFT (fish→44, wave), RIGHT (52), LEFT (44)… alternately ending at 44. Total swims until exhaustion ≈ 4: R, L, R, L → ends at 44 below the gap ✓.
Execute while watching the fish and the leading edge after each swim.

import collections
def snap(tag):
